doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How the Army changed him; Sartre and Camus
summary: Allison has little to say about the Army's effect, but Audre recalls him pressing existentialist books on her.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Elsewhere in the chapter, you speak of how being in the Army changed your perspective and your view of the world, reinforced your wanderlust. You’d majored in chemical engineering partly because you thought it might give you a chance to get out of town, and now you’d seen the world a bit, and it sounds like you came back transformed somewhat. Is there anything you can say about that, the way...
I don’t know. What should I say about...the Army?
About your personal-intellectual evolution? Or the changes in the way you thought about things, from the Army...
Well, I don’t know. I can’t... I don’t know about that now. But...
Well, I remember that when I met you, you wanted me to read Jean-Paul Sartre, Camus, Aldous Huxley, all those writers. I remember, I had to run to the library and get all those books.
